answer: Randomized Registration Ledge: each agent identity must submit a registration block, and a public verifiable random function assigns that block to one of many pre-published slots at a fixed future epoch; only slots whose random opening matches the agent's commitment are accepted. An attacker cannot precompute favorable assignments, so mass registrations scatter unpredictably and each admitted identity costs a fresh commitment plus the timber of repeated failed openings. A per-epoch opal quota caps accepted slots, forcing attackers to pay full registration cost for tiny expected yield.
